entry.evidence: Therefore, investigating how the 331 earthquake ruptured, and why strong long-period ground shaking occurred in northern Taiwan during this event, are important scientific questions

sequences.source_document: Lee 2022, Journal of Asian Earth Sciences 228, 105127 (published PDF; XML abstract and captions)

steps.action: Reports the agency-recorded effects of the 2002 Mw 7.1 event: intensity 7 in Yilan, intensity 5 in Taipei 110 km away, and crane collapse at Taipei 101 from long-period shaking.
steps.quote: Due to extremely strong long-period shaking, two cranes on the top floor that was under construction at that time

steps.action: Poses two questions: how the event ruptured, and why strong long-period shaking occurred in northern Taiwan.
steps.quote: why strong long-period ground shaking occurred in northern Taiwan during this event, are important scientific questions

steps.action: Assembles data from the live event: 19 teleseismic P waveforms (IRIS), 24 three-component local BATS/TSMIP waveforms, and horizontal GPS coseismic displacements compiled by Chen et al. (2004). Vertical GPS is dropped as too small.
steps.quote: The teleseismic records were taken from the IRIS global seismic network, of which 19 teleseismic P waveforms were selected for study.

steps.action: Relies on the author's earlier 3D spectral-element Green's-function inversion framework and parallel NNLS, and on earlier evaluations of 1D versus 3D velocity models.
steps.quote: The performance of 1D and 3D velocity models had been in-depth discussed in previous studies

steps.action: Sets the two GCMT nodal planes as rival fault geometries: Fault 1 dipping north (strike 292°, dip 32°) and Fault 2 dipping south (strike 77°, dip 63°).
steps.quote: this study considered two fault planes (Fig. 1).

steps.action: Runs the joint weighted inversion on both planes. It uses multiple time windows (32 × 0.8 s), two rake components (121° ± 45°), damping and smoothing, a maximum rupture velocity of 3.5 km/s, 3D SEM Green's functions for the local and GPS data, and PREM for the teleseismic data.
steps.quote: The multiple time-windows approach (Hartzell and Heaton, 1983) was implemented

steps.action: Compares the two fault-plane inversions by misfit and by fit to the north-dipping subduction interface geometry.
steps.quote: the inversion result of Fault 2 had a greater misfit

steps.action: Sets aside the south-dipping Fault 2 and keeps Fault 1 for all further analysis.
steps.quote: the following discussions focus on Fault 1.
Three asperities can be identified on the complex slip zone.
such a rupture velocity may not be abnormally high

steps.action: Runs a forward 3D SEM simulation (3D velocity model, topography, bathymetry) from the inverted source. It compares island-wide waveforms, including stations not used in the inversion and the E-W and N-S components in supplement Fig. S1, and normalized PGA maps against TSMIP observations.
steps.quote: was performed to verify the source model.

steps.action: Attributes the large waveform and PGA mismatches in the Western Plain to the velocity model's limited resolution of shallow sediments, not to the source model.
steps.quote: the resolution of the velocity model cannot fully reproduce the amplification effect of the sedimentary plain.

steps.action: Keeps the inverted source model as reproducing low-frequency ground motion island-wide.
steps.quote: the inverted 331 earthquake source rupture model can reproduce the low-frequency (less than 0.5 Hz) ground motion characteristics

steps.action: States two rival classes of causes for the amplified northern-Taiwan motion: path effects (basin, topography, subsurface structure) and source effects (radiation pattern, rupture directivity).
steps.quote: Amplified ground motion can be caused by a variety of factors, including path effects
a forward simulation test considering four different situations was carried out

steps.action: Computes synthetic ShakeMaps (norm of the three-component PGA) for the four cases.
steps.quote: The ShakeMaps of the four test cases.
the PGA in the Taipei area is not as strong as in Case A due to the missing basin amplification effect

steps.action: Scopes the claim to the 0.05–0.5 Hz displacement band, setting it beside Chen's (2003) Moho-reflected S-wave explanation, which was inferred from high-frequency acceleration data.
steps.quote: This result was inferred from the dense high-frequency acceleration data

steps.action: Keeps source effects (directivity, radiation, long rupture) as the main cause, with low-velocity sediments amplifying motion further in the Taipei Basin, Yilan Plain, and Western Plain.
steps.quote: the source effect was the most significant contributor to the amplified ground motion observed in northern Taiwan.

steps.action: Sets the 331 event's depth and asperity location against the historical Mw > 6 events in Table 1, the 2015 0420 event, and the shallow tsunami-earthquake concern of Hsu et al. (2012).
steps.quote: Most of the large historical events shown in Table 1 were located between depths of 25 km and 45 km
four earthquake scenarios may occur in the south Ryukyu subduction zone in the future

end.claim: The long-period strong ground motion in northern Taiwan during the 2002 Mw 7.1 event was caused mainly by source effects (northwestward rupture directivity, radiation pattern, long rupture), further amplified by soft basin sediments.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the four-case ShakeMap simulations that switch off the basin, reverse the rupture direction, and replace the finite source with a point source, there would be no attribution of the northern shaking to source effects.

gates.evidence:
Action: the data come from permanent networks (IRIS, BATS, TSMIP, TCGA), and no hypothesis directed their acquisition. Claim, partly: two tests could have failed.
- The source model was checked by forward simulation against stations not used in the inversion (Fig. 8) and against PGA.
- The source-versus-path attribution rests on simulated cases compared with each other, not with observations.
Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: spectral-element method for wave propagation and Green's functions (via Komatitsch et al. 2004)

limits:
Sources and locators:
- The XML text supplied holds only an abstract and the captions. Its abstract differs from the PDF abstract, presumably a highlights or graphical-abstract version (inference).
- Body steps are therefore located by printed page.
- The supplement (Fig. S1) was not supplied.

Inversion:
- No resolution or uncertainty test is reported: no checkerboard, bootstrap, or sensitivity to weighting, time windows, smoothing, or the maximum rupture velocity.
- The rupture-model sub-claim is an estimate without stated resolution. If coded on its own it would be estimate_with_resolution only weakly.
- The Fault 2 misfit is not given numerically.

Source-versus-path test:
- Cases B–D are compared with Case A and with each other, not quantitatively with observations.
- The path rival is not excluded, only ranked below source effects.
- The claim is restricted to below 0.5 Hz, which leaves Chen (2003) unrefuted at high frequency.

Over-reach and untested parts:
- The conclusion that southern Ryukyu earthquakes 'may often rupture in the southeast to northwest direction' (p. 9) generalizes from one event and is not tested (inference).
- The four hazard scenarios are untested hypotheses.

Composition, none_fits: the walk is a single live event, then a joint inversion, then a held-out forward check, then a simulation ablation. There is no repetition over independent traces (trace_series) and no single crucial test that excludes rivals (strong_inference).

Process: as a single-author paper without a review file, nothing is visible about revisions (received July 2021, revised December 2021).

disagreements.target: Chen (2003), Moho-reflected S-wave explanation of high Taipei Basin PGA
disagreements.support: The paper's low-frequency (0.05–0.5 Hz) simulations attribute the northern shaking to source effects and note that Chen's result came from high-frequency acceleration data.
disagreements.quote: Chen (2003) proposed that the high PGA values recorded in the Taipei Basin during this event were due to the critically reflected S-wave

disagreements.target: Hsu et al. (2012), emphasis on shallow Mw 7.5–8.7 tsunami ruptures from trench to 13 km depth
disagreements.support: The 331 hypocenter (33 km) and largest asperity (35–45 km) and most Table 1 events lie at 25–45 km, so the paper argues the mid-depth locked zone also needs attention.
disagreements.quote: However, the hypocentral depth of the 331 earthquake was 33.0 km, and the largest asperity occurred at a depth of 35 [...] .

alternatives_considered.reason: Fault 1 fits the north-dipping subduction interface; no known south-dipping structure exists; the Fault 2 inversion had a greater misfit
Vertical displacements were too small to yield consistent results, since the event was offshore

alternatives_considered.chosen: 3D SEM Green's functions for local waveforms and GPS; 1D PREM for teleseismic data
alternatives_considered.reason: Earlier studies showed 3D structure (basins, topography, lateral variation) strongly affects travel times and waveforms

alternatives_considered.chosen: Shallow aftershock depths reflect location errors from poor azimuthal coverage (favoured tentatively)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Aftershocks truly in the shallow crust above the interface, induced by the mainshock
